alternate_names: Shree Rajarajeshwari Maa Mahamaya Devi Mandir

history.dynasty: Kalachuri (claimed origin); renovated under Maratha rule
history.period: Disputed: claimed 11th century; current structure attributed to 17th-18th century renovation (verify)
history.summary: The Mahamaya Temple at Purani Basti is one of the 36 Shaktipeeths (36 forts) of Chhattisgarh and among the oldest temples in Raipur's old fort area. Dating claims CONFLICT across sources: 11th century Kalachuri (Wanderlog/reviews), 14th century, 550+ years, and Wikipedia's 'Established 17th-18th Century' with renovation by Maratha confederacy rulers; traditional attribution names Raja Mordhwaj as creator. The goddess is worshipped in Maha Kali roop; the garbhagriha has tantric architecture, and a Samaleswari shrine stands in the same compound. The temple is managed by the Shree Rajrajeshwari Maa Mahamaya Devi Mandir Raipur Trust (also cited as Sidh Shakti Peeth Shri Mahamaya Devi Mandir Trust); over 10,000 diyas are lit during the nine days of Navratri with nightly jagarata. Do not confuse with the famous Adishakti Mahamaya Temple at Ratanpur (Bilaspur district).

name: Maa Mahamaya Devi Temple, Raipur
town_description: Raipur is the capital of Chhattisgarh (since the state's formation in 2000) and its largest city, a major commercial and industrial hub of central India known for steel plants and rice milling. The old city around Purani Basti and the Kharun river preserves its pre-modern core, while newer areas like VIP Road and Naya Raipur reflect rapid recent growth. It is well connected by rail and air and serves as the gateway to Chhattisgarh's temples and national parks.
